description:
I don’t like RGB gamer lights. I find them gaudy and unnecessary, and I’ve made this point many times over my writing career. I prefer to build desktop PCs that look like tiny, classy refrigerators, not stealth fighters covered in Christmas lights. But for once, I’m actually okay with a new RGB accessory: MSI’s RGB-bedecked VESA monitor mounts. In fact, I don’t think they go far enough with it.

MSI has announced two new VESA arm models: the MPG MT201RG and MPG MT201DRG. The only difference there is a “D” in the second design, because it’s a dual-monitor stand instead of a single-arm design. Both of them have various strips of RGB lighting on the base and running up the double-sectioned arms themselves.

title: MSI’s RGB monitor arms are brilliant. They’re just not shiny enough

description:
Some of us here at PCWorld really liked Kensington’s chunky Expert Mouse TB800 EQ because it’s a comfy wireless trackball mouse with easy-to-use buttons and scroll wheels you can map to whatever functions suit your fancy.

It was also the first new iteration of the Expert Mouse that Kensington had released in roughly a decade, so there was plenty of excitement from trackball fans when it launched in 2025. That excitement quickly gave way to disappointment, as users started reporting tracking accuracy issues not long after.

Kensington, to its credit, pulled the TB800 from store shelves earlier this year and released a new model, the Expert Mouse Pro TB900 EQ. It’s nearly identical in appearance but promises to eliminate the sensor tracking issue that plagued the old TB800 EQ.
title: Expert Mouse Pro TB900 EQ tested: A better trackball at last?

description:
One of the best things about Google’s smart TV and streaming player software is that if you don’t like the standard home screen, you can replace it.

Now, you can even make the home screen look like a Roku, thanks to a free app called Kyu Launcher. This alternative home screen closely resembles Roku’s sidebar and app grid, but without any obnoxious banner ads, and it works on any Google TV or Android TV device.

Switching to Kyu Launcher takes only a couple minutes to set up, and it provides a much simpler experience whenever you press your remote’s home button. But it’s also just one of several ways to swap Google TV’s main menu for one that’s more to your liking.
title: Can’t stand Google TV? Make it look like Roku instead

description:
While opinions may differ regarding how effective AI has been to increase productivity, it’s done a far better job helping to eliminate busy work. Google Slides now can generate presentations with just a prompt, helping users to simplify a task some simply despise.

Not all meetings require a formal slide presentation to accompany discussion, but many do. Google is launching the ability to “generate presentation” from its Slides site, provided that you have the correct Business and Enterprise Standard and Plus plans on Google Workspace, or a a Google AI Pro or AI Ultra subscription. (I have neither, currently.) Otherwise, you’ll see the default slideshow view.

title: Google Slides follows PowerPoint into AI prompt-to-deck creation
